executive_summary: Entero’s September quarter combines strong organic growth, procurement scale and a higher MedTech mix. The two checks that matter are that ₹61 crore consolidated PAT includes minority interests, and that H1 operating cash flow remained negative despite the earnings improvement.
research_stance: A strengthening distribution platform, with the investment case dependent on owners’ earnings and working-capital conversion.
results_analysis: The local consolidated September 2026 quarter records revenue ₹2,087.00 crore, operating profit ₹111.00 crore and PAT ₹61.00 crore. Revenue changed +32.8% YoY and +7.6% QoQ; PAT changed +64.9% YoY and +17.3% QoQ.

Operating profit changed +79.0% YoY and +14.4% QoQ. The calculated operating-profit/sales margin is 5.32%, versus 3.95% a year earlier and 5.00% in June. These calculations use a consistently rounded local series; management EBITDA may use a different scope or definition.

The ₹61 crore local consolidated PAT is before non-controlling interests. Management puts attributable PAT at about ₹46 crore and minorities near ₹15 crore; use owners’ EPS when valuing the parent. H1 CFO of minus ₹46.5 crore, cited on the call, makes the FY27 cash-conversion guide an important uncompleted test.

Price and financial dates differ: the cleaned close used here is ₹1,971.00 on 2026-11-12; the public-financial snapshot is dated 2026-11-07. The screenshot price is not treated as a live or verified valuation input. Local public-financial-data parquets, September 2026 quarter; amounts rounded to ₹ crore.

thesis_drivers.title: Organic engine alongside acquisition calendarisation
thesis_drivers.evidence: Management separated reported growth into 18.2% organic and 14.7% inorganic growth from prior acquisitions; no acquisitions occurred in H1. This is a stronger signal than a roll-up supported only by new deals.

thesis_drivers.title: Mix and scale improve a thin-margin model
thesis_drivers.evidence: Gross margin reached 11.5% and EBITDA margin 5.3% in management commentary. Procurement economies, MedTech and deliberate withdrawal from low-margin accounts are the proposed levers; small changes have a large effect on net earnings.

thesis_drivers.title: A two-sided distribution network
thesis_drivers.evidence: Management described 92,200 retail customers, over 2,900 hospitals and more than 3,200 manufacturers across approximately 500 districts. The moat is network density and execution, not ownership of drug brands or retail consumer pricing.

valuation.method: Reverse valuation and cash-earnings constraints; no unsupported point target
valuation.assessment: The current price is roughly 62× available trailing owners’-EPS. At this valuation, profit attributed to minorities, calendarisation of acquisitions and a working-capital-supported growth spurt must not be mistaken for fully owned recurring cash earnings. The right model is attributable earnings and distributable cash after funding receivables, deferred consideration and future buyouts.
assumptions: At the 12 November adjusted close of ₹1,971.00, the available four-quarter EPS sum is ₹32.02, implying approximately 61.6× earnings and a 1.62% earnings yield. This is a price/available-EPS calculation, not a forecast or a fully normalized multiple.

A 20% contraction in the earnings multiple would require 25% cumulative EPS growth merely to keep the share price unchanged; dividends are excluded. This is algebraic sensitivity, not a prediction of the exit multiple.
A fair-value model needs an acquisition/NCI ownership bridge and cash-conversion assumptions, not consolidated total PAT multiplied by a sector P/E.

business_economics: A distributor earns a small gross margin on a large volume of goods, so procurement terms, credit losses, inventory turns and customer mix carry more economic weight than the headline revenue multiple. Q2’s 11.5% gross margin and 5.3% EBITDA margin show stronger economics, but the three stated drivers—procurement scale, MedTech mix and account pruning—have not been separated quantitatively.

18.2% organic growth is strong evidence alongside 14.7% calendarisation from earlier acquisitions. Those two engines create different future requirements: organic growth consumes working capital, while acquisitions introduce consideration payments, integration risks and minority claims.
earnings_quality: ₹61 crore consolidated PAT is not the parent’s economic earnings. The call reports ₹46 crore attributable to owners and ₹15 crore minorities; owners’ profit grew 44%, less than the 66% pre-NCI headline. An analyst should track the attributable margin and EPS, not infer parent earnings growth from consolidated total profit.

H1 CFO of–₹46.5 crore sets a demanding H2 test against the 50% full-year EBITDA-to-CFO goal. The November government collection can improve the subsequent period, but the reported September NWC remains 64 days. Repeated subsequent-event adjustments would weaken the claim of structural working-capital discipline.
capital_allocation: ₹166 crore consideration paid in H1 relates to earlier deals despite no newly completed acquisitions. Such payments are genuine funding needs and should sit beside receivable funding when assessing cash available for fresh deals or debt reduction.

Buying minorities could improve parent-attributable profit without growing consolidated PAT, but it also costs cash. Management has call-option rights and several deployment choices; the report does not assume a free or automatic transition to 100% ownership.
valuation_logic: The roughly 62× price/available-EPS ratio gives limited room for a cash-conversion shortfall. A20% multiple reduction requires 25% cumulative EPS growth just to hold price, making the ownership and cash bridge more important than achievement of a quarter’s margin.

Valuation should test three uses of cash explicitly: funding the organic sales base, settling deferred acquisition consideration, and purchasing minority stakes or new businesses. A simple acquisition-led sales CAGR does not show the residual value reaching current shareholders.
peer_positioning: Pharmacy retailers and branded manufacturers are poor direct margin benchmarks for Entero’s wholesale distribution model. Better comparisons focus on procurement scale, payable/receivable terms, credit losses, inventory expiry and ownership of acquired distributors.

The MedTech expansion broadens the economic mix but does not yet justify applying an undiluted specialty-device multiple. Product ownership, service obligations and segment profitability would have to be demonstrated separately from distribution revenue.
